title: Ultra-CAN: A Lightweight Blind ISAC Receiver for Chaos-Based Telemetry and Local-Seed Ranging in the Internet of Drones
abstract: arXiv:2611.19529v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) needs secure telemetry and proximity sensing within the SWaP-C constraints. We show that a single blind neural receiver driven by one chaos-based waveform performs both functions without a separate radar transceiver. In telemetry mode it decodes a peer's burst blindly; in radar mode it regenerates the per-burst chaotic reference locally and ranges the echoes of its own transmission. Ultra-CAN pairs a shared $64$-dimensional representation with two ultra-light backbones, an attention-pooled Conv1D network and a multi-head QKV network ($27.6$k--$44.2$k parameters), feeding communication and sensing heads. Both ship as int8 TensorFlow Lite Micro firmware; the Conv1D receiver decides a burst in $16.9$ ms on a $240$ MHz microcontroller with $24.2$ KiB of activations, a measured energy of $2.2$-$3.4$ mJ per burst, and float-equivalent decisions, sustaining up to $59$ bit/s of telemetry or a $7.4$ Hz range track. translated_title: Ultra-CAN：一种面向无人机互联网、用于基于混沌的遥测与本地种子测距的轻量级盲ISAC接收机
translated_abstract: 无人机互联网需要在SWaP-C（尺寸、重量、功耗与成本）约束下实现安全遥测与近距离感知。我们证明，由单一基于混沌的波形驱动的单个盲神经接收机可以同时完成这两项功能，而无需独立的雷达收发机。在遥测模式下，它能够盲解码对等节点的突发信号；在雷达模式下，它在本地重新生成每个突发的混沌参考信号，并对自身传输的回波进行测距。Ultra-CAN将共享的64维表示与两个超轻量骨干网络相结合——一个是注意力池化的Conv1D网络，另一个是多头QKV网络（参数量为27.6k–44.2k），为通信和感知输出头提供输入。两者均以int8 TensorFlow Lite Micro固件形式发布；Conv1D接收机在240 MHz微控制器上以24.2 KiB的激活内存、每突发2.2–3.4 mJ的实测能耗，在16.9 ms内完成一次突发判决，且决策与浮点模型等效，可支持高达59 bit/s的遥测速率或7.4 Hz的距离跟踪更新率。
tldr: Ultra-CAN提出了一种轻量级盲神经ISAC接收机，利用单一混沌波形在240 MHz微控制器上同时实现无人机的遥测盲解码与本地种子测距，无需独立雷达收发机，参数量仅27.6k–44.2k，能耗低至每突发2.2–3.4 mJ，并达到与浮点模型等效的决策性能。
en_tdlr: Ultra-CAN is a lightweight blind neural ISAC receiver that uses a single chaos-based waveform to jointly perform blind telemetry decoding and local-seed ranging for the Internet of Drones, achieving float-equivalent decisions on a 240 MHz microcontroller with only 27.6k–44.2k parameters and 2.2–3.4 mJ of energy per burst, eliminating the need for a separate radar transceiver.
